notes: Historical revenue/EBIT are sourced from StockAnalysis income statement (FY2023-FY2025). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ba/financials/))

Historical D&A and capex are sourced from StockAnalysis cash flow statement (FY2023-FY2025); capex values are reported as positive cash outflows. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ba/financials/cash-flow-statement/))

NWC is defined (for modeling consistency) as Total current assets minus Total current liabilities, using StockAnalysis balance sheet. Cash and debt are taken from Boeing’s latest FY2025 earnings press release (cash and investments in marketable securities, and consolidated debt). ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

catalysts: Sustained improvement in production quality and delivery throughput (commercial deliveries and program performance), supporting continued backlog conversion. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

Further stabilization of cash flow after PP&E investment needs decline from near-term ramp levels. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

Potential incremental contract awards or defense program execution that improves revenue visibility and margin durability. ([investors.boeing.com](https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2026/Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results/default.aspx))
company_overview: Boeing is an aerospace manufacturer and services provider with operations spanning Commercial Airplanes and Defense/Space & Security, plus Global Services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12927/000119312526096681/d23314dars.pdf))
FY2025 revenue was $89.463B with GAAP earnings from operations (EBIT) of $4.281B (EBIT margin 0.048). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ba/financials/))

FY2025 included 600 commercial deliveries and increased total company backlog to a record $682B. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))
current_context: Boeing reported FY2025 revenue of $89.463B and GAAP earnings from operations of $4.281B, reversing FY2024 operating losses. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

Total company backlog reached $682.207B, reflecting strong order flow across commercial and defense programs. ([investors.boeing.com](https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2026/Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results/default.aspx))

FY2025 operating cash flow was $1.065B and free cash flow (non-GAAP) was -$1.877B; additions to PP&E were -$2.942B. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

The company acquired Spirit AeroSystems in December 2025, reinforcing commitments to safety, quality, and production stability. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))
investment_highlights: Base case models a gradual EBIT margin recovery from FY2025 toward a normalized target margin by FY2030, consistent with an improving operating environment after FY2024 disruptions. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

Revenue growth assumptions reflect continued conversion of backlog and higher delivery volumes (FY2025 600 deliveries; backlog $682B), ramping to a mid-single-digit growth profile. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

D&A and capex are held near recent intensity to reflect ongoing production system investment and longer-cycle factory expansions. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ba/financials/cash-flow-statement/))

NWC intensity is assumed to decline modestly versus the FY2024 peak, reflecting stabilization in working-capital timing and production flow. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ba/financials/balance-sheet/))
Terminal value is anchored on an exit-multiple framework with terminal growth below long-run nominal GDP to reflect aerospace cyclicality and execution risk.
key_risks: Program execution and safety/quality events that delay deliveries or trigger charges, pushing margins below base case. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12927/000119312526096681/d23314dars.pdf))

Liquidity and capital market risk (debt servicing and working-capital volatility) if operating cash flow underperforms. ([boeing.mediaroom.com](https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-01-27-Boeing-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-Results?asPDF=1))

Pension and other long-duration obligations that can pressure future cash generation and effective tax dynamics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/12927/000119312526096681/d23314dars.pdf))

presentation.subtitle: Boeing (BA) DCF Inputs — Recovery to Mid-Cycle Margins
valuation_summary: DCF base case uses WACC 0.09 and terminal growth 0.025 with an exit EBITDA multiple (10.0) to balance Boeing-specific risk with long-run industry maturation.
Scenario framework applies realistic deltas to growth and margin recovery (bull/bear) rather than assuming abrupt normalization, helping triangulate sensitivity to execution outcomes.
Comp outputs are intentionally limited in this run due to missing free-source NTM multiple fields (set to null per schema).
